concerns.text: Synthetic queries are generated purely from the MS MARCO and DBpedia datasets without any calibration to real‑world query difficulty. Complexity level (plan depth) may be confounded with inherent difficulty (e.g., relevance distribution), threatening construct validity of the latency measure as a pure ‘structural mismatch’ effect.

The plan controls CPU time via cgroups but does not explicitly control other resources (memory pressure, I/O bandwidth) or dataset size differences across source types. These uncontrolled factors could act as confounds, making it unclear whether observed latency differences are due to structural mismatch or to disparate engine/resource characteristics.

Power analysis is asserted (≥ 0.99 for medium effect) without showing the underlying effect‑size assumptions, variance estimates, or the calculation method. A concrete power calculation (e.g., using `statsmodels.stats.power.FTestPower`) should be documented to justify the chosen sample size (1 500 queries, 200 sampled optimal).

Complexity is treated inconsistently: the ANOVA description says “categorical factor” while later the hypothesis mentions treating it as a continuous variable. This ambiguity can affect model specification and interpretation. The plan should fix complexity as either categorical (levels 1‑4+) or continuous (numeric depth) and pre‑specify the corresponding ANOVA model.

Baseline latency subtraction may produce negative corrected latencies, leading to a fallback log‑ratio transformation. This ad‑hoc handling can distort the interaction term and violate ANOVA assumptions. The plan should pre‑specify a robust baseline correction method (e.g., additive offset with floor at zero) and justify its impact on downstream inference.

The ‘reference_deviation’ flag for non‑sampled queries relies on a greedy heuristic as a proxy for ground truth. Although not used for the primary hypothesis, reporting it alongside translation_error could be misleading and may inadvertently be interpreted as a measure of accuracy. Clarify its purpose and ensure it does not influence the main analysis.
